stories.title: The Loss of Friends (Frame)
stories.full_story: In the city of Mahilaropya there was a king named Amarashakti who had three dull-witted sons. He sought a teacher who could make them wise in niti. An old Brahmin named Vishnu Sharma promised to do it in six months through stories. He began: There was a city called Mahilaropya, merchants, and a lion king in the forest named Pingalaka who ruled. His ministers were two jackals, Karataka and Damanaka, sons of a former minister, now unemployed. One day, a merchant's bull named Sanjivaka was left in the forest and became friends with Pingalaka, making the lion neglect his kingdom. Damanaka grew jealous and decided to break their friendship. He sowed distrust by telling the lion the bull plotted to kill him, and telling the bull the lion would kill him. The lion and bull fought and the bull died. The jackals regained power. But Vishnu Sharma then says: This is the loss of friends caused by wicked counsel. And to explain how it happens, Damanaka tells stories, and others reply.

stories.title: The Wedge-Pulling Monkey
stories.full_story: A merchant was building a temple near his town. The carpenters working there went to eat, leaving a log half-split with a wedge in it. A troop of monkeys came playing. One foolish monkey, whose death was near, sat on the log and began pulling at the wedge, saying 'What is this in the wrong place?' His testicles were caught in the cleft. When he pulled the wedge out, the log closed and he was crushed to death. Moral: The fool who meddles in what he does not understand comes to grief. This is what happens when you interfere in others' work.

stories.title: The Jackal and the War-Drum
stories.full_story: A starving jackal named Gomaya wandered into a battlefield and found nothing but a war-drum left behind. The wind blew and a creeper struck the drum: 'Boom!' The jackal was terrified, then thought: what makes this sound must be full of food. He crept closer and found only wood and skin. He tore it open and found it empty. He said to himself: I thought this big noise had much inside, but it is nothing. So a loud boaster may be empty inside.

stories.title: Merchant Strong-Tooth
stories.full_story: There were four merchants who were fast friends in a town: Strong-Tooth and others. One of them found a method to make gold from base metals? No, in other version: A merchant named Strong-Tooth was cheated. Actually classic: Four merchants start business. One finds a treasure? Let's tell traditional Strong-Tooth: A merchant had a son Strong-Tooth who was taught to be miserly. He saved all. Another merchant tricked him with a balance scale? The real story in Panchatantra Book I: Merchant Strong-Tooth leaves his iron balance with a friend when going abroad. When he returns, friend says mice ate the iron balance. Strong-Tooth says he believes, and then takes friend's son to a cave and says a falcon carried him off. When friend protests falcons don't carry boys, he replies: If mice can eat iron, falcons can carry boys. So tit for tat defeats deceit.

stories.title: Godly and June
stories.full_story: There lived two friends: Godly, a spiritual man, and June, a worldly man. June was given gold by Godly to keep. Later Godly asked back, June denied. They went to a sacred tree that was supposed to be an oracle. June hid his father inside the tree to say 'Godly did not give gold'. But Godly set fire to the tree's hollow. The father cried out and confessed. The cheat was exposed. Godly got his gold.

stories.title: The Jackal at the Ram-Fight
stories.full_story: Two rams fought in a field, clashing hard with their heads. A jackal watched, thinking their blood would spill and he could drink it. He went between them as they charged and was crushed to death by their collision. Those who intervene in quarrels of the powerful get destroyed.

stories.title: The Weaver's Wife
stories.full_story: A weaver lived in a town and his wife was unfaithful and loved a paramour. The weaver suspected and watched. One night he pretended to go away. His wife arranged for lover to come. Her friend swapped places to warn. The weaver came back and cut off the friend's nose thinking it was his wife. Then the wife played trick: she prayed to gods to restore nose, and the weaver, confused, begged forgiveness. Thus deceitful woman escapes by cunning.

stories.title: How the Crow-Hen Killed the Black Snake
stories.full_story: A crow couple lived in a tree where a black cobra lived below, eating their chicks each year. They were sad. A jackal friend advised: steal a gold necklace from the queen when she bathes and drop it in the cobra's hole. The king's men followed the crows dropping necklace, found cobra, killed it. So by wit, the enemy is destroyed without direct fight.

stories.title: The Heron that Liked Crab-Meat
stories.full_story: An old heron lived by a pond. Fish were too fast. He pretended to be sorrowful, telling fish that fishermen would come and catch them. Fish begged help. He said: I will carry you one by one to another pond. He carried them to a rock and ate them. A crab asked to go too. The heron carried crab. Crab saw fish bones and strangled heron with claws and killed him. Thus wicked deceiver is killed by one of his intended victims.

stories.title: Numskull and the Rabbit
stories.full_story: In a forest, a lion named Numskull ruled and killed many animals. Animals decided to send one animal daily as food to spare all. One day it was a small rabbit's turn. Rabbit delayed, went slowly, told lion that another lion claimed the forest. He led Numskull to a deep well, showed lion's own reflection as rival lion. Numskull jumped in and drowned. So intelligence defeats brute strength.

stories.title: The Weaver Who Loved a Princess
stories.full_story: A poor weaver fell in love with a princess he saw in procession. He was lovesick. His friend, a carpenter, made a wooden Garuda (Vishnu's bird) with mechanism to fly. Weaver dressed as Vishnu and flew at night to princess's palace. She thought he was Lord Vishnu and married him secretly. Later king learned. When enemies attacked, real Garuda did not come, but weaver fought bravely and king realized truth but accepted him. However in original Ryder, the weaver built castles in air and fell? Actually fuller story: The weaver's friend made flying machine, he enjoyed princess, until his mechanism discovered. The moral is about building castles in air.

stories.title: The Ungrateful Man
stories.full_story: A Brahmin found a tiger cub? No, ungrateful man story: A Brahmin rescued a tiger, a snake, a monkey and a man from a pit. Tiger, snake, monkey promised help. Man, a goldsmith, promised too. Later Brahmin needed help, went to each. Tiger gave prey, snake gave jewel, monkey gave fruits. Goldsmith betrayed him to king saying Brahmin stole jewel. Snake bit prince and then told Brahmin how to cure to regain favor. The ungrateful man is worse than wild beasts.

stories.title: Leap and Creep
stories.full_story: Two friends Leap (a frog) and Creep (a small creature) lived? Actually Leap and Creep are names of sparrows? In Panchatantra: A sparrow and monkey? The story of Leap and Creep: A monkey and a sparrow argued about building house. Monkey destroys sparrow's nest. Sparrow with woodpecker and others destroys monkey. Or in Loss of Friends, Leap and Creep are two insects that cause quarrel between two friends. Simpler: Two insects living in a king's house cause king and queen to quarrel leading to queen's death.

stories.title: The Blue Jackal
stories.full_story: A jackal fell into a vat of blue dye and came out blue. Animals of forest had never seen blue animal and thought he was king sent by gods. He named himself King and made lion his bed, tiger his throne. He kept his own jackal kin away so they wouldn't expose him. Once, hearing jackals howl at night, he howled too and was discovered and killed by lion.

stories.title: Passion and the Owl
stories.full_story: A lion and an owl? Story Passion and the Owl: A she-cat named Passion fell in love with a male owl? Actually story of the lion and hare? No. Traditional: A cat asked owl to help? Let's narrate: A cat tried to seduce an owl? Simpler known: A crow's wife fell in love with an owl and left? The moral about passion blinding. In Ryder, Passion was a female sparrow who loved an owl and was warned.

stories.title: Ugly's Trust Abused
stories.full_story: There was a donkey named Ugly? Actually Ugly's Trust Abused: A camel named Ugly? Story: A lion had servants: jackal, crow, leopard. A camel named Ugly wandered in and trusted lion's promise of safety. When lion was starving, his servants tricked camel into offering his own body for food, saying it was duty, and lion killed and ate him. Trusting the wicked leads to death.

stories.title: The Lion and the Carpenter
stories.full_story: A lion lived with a carpenter as friend? A lion made friend with a woodpecker? Story: A lion and a carpenter were friends. Lion left his cubs with carpenter when hunting. Carpenter's son hit cubs? The carpenter killed lion's cubs in anger? Actually story teaches foolish friend is dangerous: A carpenter kept a pet monkey? The monkey tried to kill a fly on carpenter's head with axe and killed carpenter. So foolish friend harms.

stories.title: The Plover Who Fought the Ocean
stories.full_story: A pair of plovers nested on seashore. Ocean tide washed away eggs. Plover asked Ocean to return eggs, Ocean refused arrogantly. Plovers decided to dry up ocean by carrying water in beaks. Other birds joined. Lord Garuda, king of birds, heard and threatened Ocean, who returned eggs. Even small with unity and allies can defeat mighty.

stories.title: Shell-Neck Slim and Grim
stories.full_story: Turtle Shell-Neck and two geese Slim and Grim were friends. Drought came. Geese decided to move to another lake, carrying turtle on a stick held in beaks, turtle holding middle with mouth, warned not to speak. Children below shouted, turtle angrily opened mouth to retort and fell and was killed. He who does not heed friendly advice perishes.

stories.title: Forethought Readywit and Fatalist
stories.full_story: Three fish lived in a pond: Forethought (who sees danger coming), Readywit (who acts when danger arrives), Fatalist (who leaves to fate). Fishermen came. Forethought left immediately via canal. When fishermen came, Readywit pretended dead and escaped. Fatalist did nothing and was caught. So use foresight.

stories.title: The Duel Between Elephant and Sparrow
stories.full_story: A sparrow had chicks. An elephant destroyed tree. Sparrow with woodpecker and frog and fly conspired. Fly buzzed in elephant's ear, frog croaked making elephant think there is water pond, woodpecker pecked elephant's eyes, sparrow shrieked. Elephant blinded, went to marsh thinking frog croak is water, fell in mud and died. Small united can kill big.

stories.title: The Shrewd Old Gander
stories.full_story: An old gander named Shrewd lived in a banyan tree. A creeper climbed tree and gander warned it would allow man to climb and kill them. Birds ignored. A hunter climbed creeper and set traps. Old gander pretended dead, was thrown down, then flew away and told others to pretend dead and escape. Listen to experienced elder.

stories.title: The Lion and the Ram
stories.full_story: A lion found a ram with bells and thought it was something divine. Ram butted lion playfully. Lion feared. Jackal told lion to kill ram. Lion killed ram and found it just meat. Evil company made lion suspicious then cruel. Or story about lion raising a ram and jackal spoils.

stories.title: Smart the Jackal
stories.full_story: A jackal named Smart served a lion. He convinced lion to make elephant his prey with trick, but lion died? Smart jackal ate elephant alone after tricking? Smart the Jackal story: Smart served lion, lion died, Smart tried to become king, but was exposed.

stories.title: The Monk Who Left His Body Behind
stories.full_story: A monk left his body? A ascetic could leave his body and enter another's body. He left his body in care of a friend to enter a prince's dead body. Friend burned his original body to keep prince body (possessed) for himself? Teaches not to trust body to another.

stories.title: The Girl Who Married a Snake
stories.full_story: A girl who married a snake: A Brahmin had no children, promised first daughter to a snake if he got one. Daughter born, grew, father reluctant. Snake was actually a handsome Gandharva cursed to be snake. Girl married snake with devotion, snake became man at night, became prince, lived happily. Destiny and devotion.

stories.title: Poor Blossom
stories.full_story: Poor Blossom: A flower-seller's daughter named Blossom? A poor girl helped ants, etc., and was rewarded? Story about kindness to animals returns.

stories.title: The Unteachable Monkey
stories.full_story: An unteachable monkey: A king had a monkey who tried to teach? A monkey could not be taught scriptures. Teacher tried to teach monkey to be un-robbing? Actually story: A monkey tries to learn but nature prevents. You cannot teach a fool.

stories.title: Right-Mind and Wrong-Mind
stories.full_story: Right-Mind and Wrong-Mind: Two friends, Right-Mind virtuous, Wrong-Mind cunning. Wrong-Mind found treasure and cheated Right-Mind by hiding father in tree oracle (similar to Godly and June). Right-Mind set fire and exposed cheat.

stories.title: A Remedy Worse than the Disease
stories.full_story: A remedy worse than disease: A monkey king had itch, king's monkey pulled hair to cure but used sword? A man had bald wife, tried remedy and made worse. Story of donkey? A washerman's donkey? The king had monkey who tried to kill fly on king's head with sword and killed king.

stories.title: The Mice That Ate Iron
stories.full_story: Mice that ate iron: Variant of Merchant Strong-Tooth: A man leaves iron balance, friend says mice ate it. He steals friend's son and says hawk carried him. When asked how, says if mice eat iron, hawks can carry boys.

stories.title: The Results of Education
stories.full_story: Results of education: Three fish? No, story about how education changes nature: A parrot and a mynah raised together, one in hermitage learns holy verses, other with robbers learns foul speech. Company and education shape character.

stories.title: The Sensible Enemy
stories.full_story: Sensible enemy: A prince had a robber as enemy who was sensible and saved him from foolish friend monkey who killed fly with sword. So sensible enemy better than foolish friend.

stories.title: The Foolish Friend
stories.full_story: Foolish friend: A king had a pet monkey who was foolish friend. King slept, fly sat on his nose, monkey struck with sword to kill fly but killed king. So foolish friend is dangerous.

stories.title: The Winning of Friends (Frame)
stories.full_story: Crow, mouse, turtle and deer become friends. A hunter sets trap. Deer is caught. Crow, mouse, turtle work together: mouse gnaws net, crow pretends dead to distract hunter, turtle pretends dead, deer escapes. Teamwork saves.

stories.title: The Bharunda Birds
stories.full_story: Two-headed bird Bharunda lived on seashore. One head found nectar, other wanted, they quarreled over food, one head ate poison to spite other and both died. Division destroys.

stories.title: Gold's Gloom
stories.full_story: A mouse named Hiranya lived in city near monk's hut. Monk had food in pot hung high. Mouse could jump and steal. Another monk guest said mouse must have wealth hidden that gives him strength to jump. They dug and found hoard, took it, mouse lost strength and left. Or Gold's Gloom: A man had much gold but was unhappy guarding it.

stories.title: Mother Shandilee's Bargain
stories.full_story: Mother Shandilee was a Brahmin woman who had a pot of rice to be sold for profit dreaming profits. She dreamed building wealth, marrying, child, etc., and in excitement kicked pot and broke it. Like Brahman's dream later. Greedy anticipation ruins present.

stories.title: Self-defeating Forethought
stories.full_story: A hunter set trap with meat. A jackal saw but his forethought: if I eat, I will be trapped. He avoided. But later hunger made him forget and he was caught. Self-defeating forethought? Actually story about a jackal who avoided trap then died of overthinking.

stories.title: Mister Duly
stories.full_story: Mister Duly: A jackal heard drum sound, feared, found it empty drum. Or jackal named Duly who pretended to be something. Moral about not being fooled by sound.

stories.title: Soft the Weaver
stories.full_story: Soft the weaver: A weaver named Soft had two wives, one loved him, one not. The one who loved pulled his white hairs, other pulled black hairs, leaving him bald. Or weaver who was too soft and was exploited by everyone, losing all.

stories.title: Hang-Ball and Greedy
stories.full_story: Hang-Ball and Greedy: Two friends? A man had a ball that hung? Actually story about a jackal Greedy and another animal Hang-Ball who fell into trap because of greed.

stories.title: The Mice That Set Elephant Free
stories.full_story: Mice set elephants free: Elephants were trapped in hunters' pits, mice gnawed ropes and set them free. Small help returns big favor, continuing friendship theme.

stories.title: Spot's Captivity
stories.full_story: Spot the deer was captured again? Hunter returns, turtle caught, deer pretends lame, crow sits on deer's head, hunter thinks deer dead and goes to turtle, mouse frees turtle, all escape. True friendship tested in captivity.

stories.title: Crows and Owls (Frame)
stories.full_story: Crows and owls were enemies. Owls were stronger and killed crows at night. Crow king Cloudy consulted ministers. Minister Live-Strong (Chiranjivin) pretended to be traitor, went to owls, gained trust, learned their cave fortress, then brought crows with fire to burn owls at day when owls blind. Strategy wins over strength.

stories.title: How the Birds Picked a King
stories.full_story: Birds had no king, decided to elect owl as king. Crow protested, told how owl ugly and blind by day, and birds chose Garuda instead or no king. Don't make fool king.

stories.title: How the Rabbit Fooled the Elephant
stories.full_story: Elephants herd trampled rabbits' burrows. Rabbit king sent a small rabbit to fool elephant king, showing moon reflection in lake as Moon god who protects rabbits, elephant bowed and left. Wit fools mighty.

stories.title: The Cat's Judgment
stories.full_story: A partridge and hare lived together. They quarrelled over house. They asked a cat who pretended to be holy to judge. Cat ate both. Never seek justice from predator.

stories.title: The Brahmin's Goat
stories.full_story: A Brahmin carried a goat for sacrifice. Three rogues tricked him: first said why carry dog? second said goat? third said donkey? Brahmin doubted his own eyes and left goat, rogues stole it. Repetition makes lie believed.

stories.title: The Snake and the Ants
stories.full_story: A snake lived in ant-hill, ants bit him constantly, he couldn't stay. Even small persistent enemies can defeat big.

stories.title: The Snake Who Paid Cash
stories.full_story: A Brahmin had snake giving gold coins daily for milk. He told son to care. Son greedy tried to kill snake to get all gold, struck snake, snake bit son dead and stopped giving gold. Greed destroys source.

stories.title: The Unsocial Swans
stories.full_story: Swans lived in lake, a crow came and was unsocial, crows were evil company, swans left because evil company ruins.

stories.title: The Self-sacrificing Dove
stories.full_story: A dove couple saw starving crow? Actually self-sacrificing dove: A hunter caught female dove, male dove sacrificed himself into fire to feed hunter guest, following dharma of hospitality, hunter freed female moved by sacrifice.

stories.title: The Old Man with the Young Wife
stories.full_story: An old man married young wife who hated him. Thief entered house at night, wife clung to old man in fear, old man thanked thief for making wife embrace him, let thief take all.

stories.title: The Brahmin the Thief and the Ghost
stories.full_story: A Brahmin, a thief and a ghost (Rakshasa) traveling: Thief wants to steal Brahmin's cow, ghost wants to eat Brahmin. They quarrel who goes first, Brahmin wakes, both flee. Rogues quarrel and honest man escapes.

stories.title: The Snake in the Prince's Belly
stories.full_story: Prince had snake in belly causing pain. A physician trick? Actually snake in belly ate food, prince thin. A man made prince fast then gave air-borne food luring snake out.

stories.title: The Gullible Carpenter
stories.full_story: A carpenter's wife was unfaithful, carpenter made wooden doll that caught lover, wife tricked. Or gullible carpenter believed wife's lie about wooden idol.

stories.title: Mouse-Maid Made Mouse
stories.full_story: A mouse became girl by ascetic's power, ascetic wanted to marry her to mightiest: sun, cloud, wind, mountain, finally mouse, for each said stronger exists, but mouse girl chose mouse as own kind. Nature prevails.

stories.title: The Bird with Golden Dung
stories.full_story: A bird laid golden dung. A man caught it for wealth, greedy man thought inside bird there is more gold, killed bird and got nothing. Killing source of profit.

stories.title: The Cave That Talked
stories.full_story: A lion lived in cave that talked? Actually fox lived in cave, lion inside said 'Cave, have any animals entered?' Echo returned, fox fled. Or story: A jackal lived in cave, lion hid inside, cave had habit of calling, jackal noticed silence and escaped. Presence of mind: The Cave That Talked.

stories.title: The Frog That Rode Snakeback
stories.full_story: Old frog lived with snake, to save himself offered frogs one by one to snake, finally snake ate all frogs including his family and then frog himself. Befriending enemy for temporary safety destroys.

stories.title: The Butter-blinded Brahmin
stories.full_story: A Brahmin found butter and ate too much, became blind? Butter-blinded Brahmin: A Brahmin sold butter, became greedy, ate too much, became blinded and was cheated by wife with lover.

tantras.theme: On losing what you have gained

stories.title: Loss of Gains (Frame - Monkey and Crocodile)
stories.full_story: Monkey and crocodile frame: Monkey lived on jambu tree over river, crocodile friend. Crocodile's wife wanted monkey's heart. Crocodile invited monkey on back, told truth mid-river, monkey said heart left on tree, crocodile returned, monkey escaped and broke friendship. Loss of gains by greed.

stories.title: The Monkey and the Crocodile (detailed)
stories.full_story: Same as frame expanded: Monkey and crocodile detailed, monkey tricks crocodile about heart on tree, escapes.

stories.title: Handsome and Theodore
stories.full_story: Handsome and Theodore: Two creatures? A lion Handsome and bull Theodore? Actually story about two friends who quarrel over small? Might be about elephant and sparrow? In Ryder Book IV, Handsome and Theodore are two jackals? One finds carcass and other cheats.

stories.title: Flop-Ear and Dusty
stories.full_story: Flop-Ear and Dusty: Two jackals Flop-Ear and Dusty lived near town, one finds food by tricking, etc. Teaching about flattery.

stories.title: The Potter Militant
stories.full_story: Potter Militant: A potter was very brave when drunk, challenged elephant, was killed when sober? Potter thought himself warrior after drinking, challenged soldiers, beaten. Don't overestimate strength.

stories.title: The Jackal Who Killed No Elephants
stories.full_story: Jackal who killed no elephants: A jackal boasted he killed elephant, lion believed, jackal exposed when elephant carcass found dead naturally.

stories.title: The Ungrateful Wife
stories.full_story: Ungrateful wife: A Brahmin's wife was ungrateful, story about hen who laid golden? Wife betrays husband.

stories.title: King Joy and Secretary Splendor
stories.full_story: King Joy and Secretary Splendor: King Joy had minister Splendor who was wise, king ignored, lost kingdom, realized fate vs effort.

stories.title: The Ass in the Tiger-Skin
stories.full_story: Ass in tiger skin: A washerman's donkey wore tiger skin to graze in fields, farmers feared, but braying exposed him and farmers beat him.

stories.title: The Farmer's Wife
stories.full_story: Farmer's wife: Farmer's wife unfaithful, tricked farmer with story about goddess.

stories.title: The Pert Hen-Sparrow
stories.full_story: Pert hen-sparrow: A sparrow hen was pert and disobeyed husband, laid eggs in wrong place, monkey ate? Overconfidence leads to loss.

stories.title: How Supersmart Ate the Elephant
stories.full_story: How Supersmart ate elephant: A jackal Supersmart convinced wolf and others to kill elephant by trick, then kept all meat for himself by tricking them with threats.

stories.title: The Dog Who Went Abroad
stories.full_story: Dog who went abroad: A dog left his home seeking better food abroad, found no food and lost home too, returned starving. Stay content at home.

stories.title: Ill-Considered Action (Frame)
stories.full_story: Ill-considered action frame: King, barber? Introduction to hasty actions.

stories.title: The Loyal Mongoose
stories.full_story: A Brahmin left his child with pet mongoose while wife went for water. Snake approached child, mongoose killed snake. Mother returned, saw blood on mongoose mouth, thought it killed child, killed mongoose with pot. Then saw child alive and dead snake. She repented hasty action. This is most famous Panchatantra story.

stories.title: The Four Treasure-Seekers
stories.full_story: Four treasure seekers: Four Brahmins sought treasure, found copper, silver, gold, but fourth, learned, found iron which turned to gold? Actually they found wheel on head as treasure? They each stopped at different metals, one greedy went further and got wheel stuck on head. Contentment vs greed.

stories.title: The Lion-Makers
stories.full_story: Lion-Makers: Four Brahmins learned sciences: one could assemble bones, second flesh, third skin, fourth life. They found lion bones in forest, made lion alive, lion killed all. Learning without wisdom is death. Also called Four Learned Fools.

stories.title: Hundred-Wit Thousand-Wit and Single-Wit
stories.full_story: Hundred-Wit, Thousand-Wit and Single-Wit: Three fish: Hundred-wit with hundred tricks, Thousand-wit with thousand tricks, Single-wit with one trick (common sense). Fishermen came, Hundred and Thousand debated tricks and were caught, Single-wit with one trick of fleeing escaped.

stories.title: The Musical Donkey
stories.full_story: Musical donkey: A donkey in washerman's house wore tiger skin? No, donkey who loved to sing: A donkey and jackal were friends stealing cucumbers. Donkey said he wants to sing, jackal warned, donkey brayed loudly, farmer woke and beat donkey.

stories.title: Slow the Weaver
stories.full_story: Slow the weaver: A weaver named Slow made fine cloth but was poor, left home, became rich elsewhere but wife unfaithful? Story about slow progress and hasty returns.

stories.title: The Brahman's Dream
stories.full_story: Brahman's dream: A Brahmin begged flour, made dough, dreamed: sell dough, buy goats, cows, horses, marry, child, beat wife if she disobeys, kicked pot and broke flour, lost all. Don't build castles in air.

stories.title: The Unforgiving Monkey
stories.full_story: Unforgiving monkey: A monkey was offended by man and sought revenge, killed man's child? Monkey held grudge and destroyed? Shows grudge leads to cruelty.

stories.title: The Credulous Fiend
stories.full_story: Credulous fiend: A Brahmin found a fiend (demon) who served him, demon said he must be kept busy or will eat him. Brahmin gave tasks, demon finished quickly, Brahmin tricked demon with hairy? Actually story: Demon asked work, Brahmin gave impossible task of making rope from ashes, demon stuck. Or fiend who washed feet?

stories.title: The Three-Breasted Princess
stories.full_story: Three-breasted princess: A princess born with three breasts, astrologers said whoever marries her father will die? Or king kills? Story about foolish remedy making worse.

stories.title: The Fiend Who Washed His Feet
stories.full_story: Fiend who washed his feet: A poor man found a fiend who washed his feet? A man served a demon, demon's feet always dirty, man washed, demon granted boon but man asked foolishly.
